title: Signature Doc-Lineage Binding
description: Signature edition: every documentation page is cryptographically bound to the exact code commit it describes. Readers see the commit hash and can verify the docs match that code; when code moves on, the binding visibly breaks until docs are re-synced. Documentation carries proof of what it documents. This is a Signature original method.
method: Doc builds record the code commit hash and per-page source hashes; the rendered page displays and links them; a verifier re-checks bindings on every code change.
usage: Emit bindings at doc build time; surface broken bindings as sync tasks, not silent rot.

title: Signature Doctest executable examples
description: Signature edition: Doctests embed runnable examples in docstrings that the test suite actually executes. Documentation examples can't go stale because they're tests: if the code changes behavior, the doctest fails and someone must update both. Python's doctest module and Rust's doc-tests prove docs by running them.
method: Write examples as doctest format in docstrings; the test runner executes them and compares output; failures block the merge.
usage: Write examples for every public function; keep expected outputs exact; run doctests in CI.

demo.code:
import doctest
def add(a, b):
    '''Add.
    >>> add(2, 3)
    5
    '''
    return a + b
print('doctest:', doctest.testmod(verbose=False))

title: Signature Doc-coverage gates
description: Signature edition: Coverage gates measure what fraction of public symbols have documentation and fail the build below a threshold. Like test coverage, the number isn't the point — the gate is: it makes undocumented public API a conscious, visible choice rather than an accident.
method: Count public symbols vs documented ones; compute coverage; fail CI below threshold; track the trend over time.
usage: Set the threshold at your current level, then ratchet it up; exempt internal APIs explicitly.

demo.code:
documented, total = 45, 50
cov = documented / total
print(f'doc coverage {cov:.0%} ->', 'PASS' if cov >= 0.9 else 'FAIL: document 5 more symbols')

title: Signature Tutorial testing (executable guides)
description: Signature edition: Tutorials rot faster than API docs because they describe sequences. Executable tutorials run every step as a test — create the project, run the commands, assert the outputs — so a tutorial that no longer works fails CI instead of misleading users.
method: Encode tutorial steps as scripts with assertions; run in a clean container on CI; any step failure marks the tutorial stale.
usage: Keep tutorials' setup hermetic; pin versions; treat tutorial CI as seriously as unit tests.

demo.code:
steps = [('create project', True), ('run build', True), ('assert output', True)]
print('tutorial test:', 'PASS' if all(s[1] for s in steps) else 'STALE')

title: Signature Diagram-as-code synchronization
description: Signature edition: Architecture diagrams drawn by hand die with the first refactor. Diagram-as-code (Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz) lives in the repo, renders in CI, and can be generated from the code itself (dependency graphs from imports, sequence diagrams from traces) — diagrams that can't drift because they're built from the source of truth.
method: Author diagrams in text; render in CI; optionally generate structural diagrams from code analysis; embed rendered output in docs.
usage: Ban binary diagram files; generate what can be generated; hand-author only what can't.

demo.code:
print('```mermaid')
print('graph LR; A[api] --> B[db]; A --> C[cache]')
print('```')
print('rendered in CI from repo text; dependency graph generated from imports')

title: Signature Doc search index rebuild
description: Signature edition: Documentation is useless if unfindable. The synchronizer rebuilds the full-text search index on every docs deploy — new pages appear in search immediately, renamed pages don't leave ghost results, and the index always matches the published docs exactly.
method: Crawl built docs; extract text per page; build the index (Lunr, Pagefind, Algolia); deploy index with docs atomically.
usage: Rebuild the index in the same pipeline as the docs; never deploy docs without their index.

title: Signature Changelog generation from commits
description: Signature edition: Changelogs written by hand rot; changelogs generated from conventional commits (feat:, fix:, BREAKING CHANGE:) are always complete. Release tooling groups commits by type, links issues, and drafts release notes — the changelog becomes a deterministic function of history.
method: Enforce conventional-commit format; on release, collect commits since last tag; group by type; render markdown; attach to the release.
usage: Lint commit messages in CI; generate the changelog at release time, never by hand.

demo.code:
commits = [('feat', 'add search'), ('fix', 'null crash'), ('feat', 'dark mode')]
from collections import Counter
print('changelog groups:', dict(Counter(t for t, _ in commits)))

title: Signature OpenAPI spec sync from code
description: Signature edition: API documentation drifts fastest at the HTTP boundary. Generating the OpenAPI spec from route handlers and type annotations (FastAPI, Springdoc) makes the spec, the docs UI, and the validation logic all derive from one source — change the handler and the docs follow automatically.
method: Decorate handlers with types; the framework emits OpenAPI JSON at runtime; docs UI (Swagger/ReDoc) renders it; contract tests validate the spec against live traffic.
usage: Type your handlers completely; serve the spec from the app; add contract tests that fail on spec/traffic mismatch.

title: Signature Documentation drift detection
description: Signature edition: Drift detectors compare docs against code and flag mismatches: documented parameters that no longer exist, new parameters nobody documented, examples that no longer run. Running as a CI check, drift detection turns 'docs are outdated' from a complaint into a failing build.
method: Extract documented signature from docs; extract actual signature from code; diff; report missing/extra/changed items as CI failures or warnings.
usage: Run on every PR touching public APIs; start as warnings, graduate to failures once the backlog is clean.

demo.code:
documented, actual = {'a', 'b'}, {'a', 'b', 'c'}
print('drift: undocumented params =', actual - documented, '-> CI warning')
